items.followUp: State two postulates of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: The positively charged nucleus is a central postulate of Rutherford’s model.
rubric.description: Identifies the small, positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for describing the nucleus as small and positively charged, and placing it at the centre.

rubric.why: This states how electrons are arranged and move in the model.
rubric.description: States that electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying electrons and their motion around the nucleus.

rubric.why: This gives a further feature of the model or the force involved in electron motion.
rubric.description: States that electrostatic attraction holds electrons around the nucleus, or that most of the atom is empty space.

modelAnswer: An atom has a very small, dense, positively charged nucleus at its centre; nearly all the mass of the atom is concentrated in it.
Electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths.
Electrostatic attraction between the nucleus and electrons holds them together, and most of the atom is empty space.

items.followUp: Write any four properties of a mixture.

rubric.why: Mixture components are not present in a fixed ratio.
rubric.description: States that a mixture has variable composition or that its components may be present in any proportion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for variable composition or any proportion.

rubric.why: The components keep their individual identities in a mixture.
rubric.description: States that the components retain their individual properties.

rubric.why: Mixture components can be separated without a chemical reaction.
rubric.description: States that the components can be separated by physical methods.

rubric.why: A mixture does not have the definite melting or boiling point of a pure substance.
rubric.description: States that a mixture has no fixed melting point or boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct statement.

modelAnswer: A mixture has variable composition; its components may be present in any proportion.
The components retain their individual properties.
The components can be separated by physical methods.
A mixture has no fixed melting point or boiling point.
